entries.answer: Hello! I can answer questions about the figures on this dashboard: total value, daily and period returns, benchmark comparison, asset allocation and stock breakdown.

You can ask about the fund's total portfolio value, its daily return, the cumulative return for the period you selected, the gap against the benchmark, the asset allocation, the heaviest stock positions, and which date the figures belong to.
A basis point (bps) is one hundredth of a percent, so 100 bps equals 1%. We show the benchmark gap in basis points because it states small differences precisely.
The benchmark is the reference index the fund's performance is measured against. When the fund's return is above the benchmark, it outperformed its reference over that period.
Cumulative return is the total percentage return built up from the start of the period to the data date. It is not the plain sum of daily returns; it includes compounding.

keywords: why is the stock breakdown old
entries.answer: The stock breakdown comes from the fund's portfolio disclosure period and is updated monthly, so it can belong to an older period than the other figures.
